title: [Feature] Full Account Backup & Restore
body:
### Problem / motivation

Currently there is no built-in way to back up and restore accounts and configuration. When migrating to a new server, reinstalling Codex-LB, or recovering from a failure, users have to manually recreate their accounts and settings.

### Proposed change

Add a Backup & Restore feature that allows users to:
- Export all configured accounts and settings to a backup file.
- Import a backup file to restore accounts and settings.
- Perform backup and restore operations from the web UI.

### Alternatives considered

Manual database backups and manual reconfiguration. However, these approaches are less convenient and more error-prone, especially for non-technical users.


### Additional context

This feature would simplify server migrations, upgrades, and disaster recovery by providing an easy way to preserve and restore account data and configuration.

title: feat(accounts): add per-account usage limits
head: caf31b77a4ef85047459635e956fdd62f7fbd7ce
body: ## Summary Reserve part of each account's standard quota for direct use, with a shared default and optional independent 5-hour and weekly limits. The same normalized policy governs admission, account quota bars, dashboard credits, and weekly pace. Fixes #631. Consolidates the complementary controls and reserve presentation from #2147, following the maintainer's [reconciliation requirements](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/pull/2147#issuecomment-5612810413), with credit to aaravrav. ## Changes - Existing scalar policies retain their meaning. The feature defaults off, requires no new setup, and adds no settings or navigation items. Disable retains saved values atomically; removal clears them. Overrides match reported duration, while monthly windows use the shared default. - Enabled policies gate ordinary, sticky, additional-quota, HTTP bridge, WebSocket, and synthetic-warmup admission. Missing or stale required telemetry fails closed. Already dispatched work retains its owner and settlement. Delayed provider reporting can still overshoot the observed cap. - Final selection fences cover recovery-probe commitment and initial process-seed persistence. Rejected WebSocket frames retain tracked finalization ownership through cancellation; late selection exits reuse cancellation-deferring cleanup. Committed affinity and existing error contracts are preserved. - Fresh final owner checks distinguish policy denial (HTTP 429 / `rate_limit_error`, without an upstream reset deadline) from authorization infrastructure failure. Dispatch preparation, cancellation cleanup, and committed telemetry invalidation retain their documented boundaries. - Warmup authorization uses transient projections so settlement cannot overwrite a newer operator edit. Quota warmup reuses its resolved settings snapshot without another settings wait after final authorization. - Preserve both published and reviewed local histories on newest upstream. Retain the original scalar migration parent and join the upstream and override lineages with explicit merges, yielding one upgrade head. Historical-schema upgrades preserve saved defaults and overrides; branch-specific downgrades retain unrelated lineage. - Show provider remaining, reserved, and usable quota together. Remove unused policy/cache remnants and update the existing urllib3 dependency to 2.8.0 for the Docker security scan. ## OpenSpec and validation Normative contracts: [account routing](openspec/specs/account-routing/spec.md), [warmup](openspec/specs/proxy-warmup/spec.md), [quota planner](openspec/specs/quota-phase-planner/spec.md), and [migrations](openspec/specs/database-migrations/spec.md). Verification details and architectural rationale are retained in the archived feature and review changes under `openspec/changes/archive/`. - Three independent concurrency regressions reproduced the failures before fixes; coverage exercises acknowledged policy mutations and durable warmup settlement. - Historical local/published-schema upgrade tests and all four overflow/transport direct-downgrade cases pass. Migration checks report one canonical head and no schema drift. - Earlier full feature validation: frontend coverage: 1,704 tests across 185 files. Backend lint, typing, frontend lint/types/build, simplicity budgets, and strict OpenSpec validation pass. - Earlier independent changed-backend-module sweep: 4,715 passed / 38 skipped. Isolated lifespan tests: 49 passed. Focused concurrency regressions: 18 passed / 8 PostgreSQL-only skips. Local PostgreSQL is unavailable; current-head cloud CI verifies that backend separately. - This correction: 830 routing/Responses/migration tests passed with 11 PostgreSQL-only skips; 454 transport/cancellation tests, 436 additional WebSocket tests, and four historical migration-merge cases passed (1,724 backend passes total). All seven new schedules pass; six reproduce the defects on the original head. Existing regression assertions are retained. - This correction: lint, typing, Rust checks/audit, frontend lint/types/build, package assets, and strict validation of all 67 specifications passed. Fresh upstream is already an ancestor; topology reports 267 revisions and one head, and SQLite upgrade/check reports no drift. No new migration is added. - The full local gate stopped on two coverage-enabled frontend cases (1,702 passed). Both cases passed without coverage and failed again with coverage; no frontend source is changed by this correction. On published head `caf31b77a4ef85047459635e956fdd62f7fbd7ce`, full cloud CI subsequently passed, including frontend coverage, all integration shards, PostgreSQL, both migration checks, Docker, Helm, Nix, and `CI Required`. Current-head status has 35 successes, one expected Pages deployment skip, one neutral security check, and no failed or pending checks. CodeRabbit reviewed this exact head and reported no new actionable comments; all 68 review threads are resolved. GitHub reports `MERGEABLE` / `CLEAN`. Maintainer review/merge remains pending. ## Before / after Before: the scalar limit editor from the previous PR version. After: shared reserve plus optional per-window reserves. Blank values inherit the shared reserve; disable and remove remain separate actions. ![Combined reserve editor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NikitaMGrimm/codex-lb/52f86b3a9c4c714154ec89e400579b0b1006f3a8/reserve-editor.png) Provider remaining bars retain their direction. Hatched reserve is on the left, available quota next, and consumed quota on the right; summaries sit below reset times. ![Account reserve display](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NikitaMGrimm/codex-lb/52f86b3a9c4c714154ec89e400579b0b1006f3a8/accounts-window-reserves.png) Dashboard centers show usable credits, hatching identifies reserved quota, and weekly pace uses the effective capacity while retaining the provider-scale observed burn rate. ![Reserved and usable dashboard credits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NikitaMGrimm/codex-lb/52f86b3a9c4c714154ec89e400579b0b1006f3a8/dashboard-reserves.png) All after screenshots use synthetic local accounts. > [!NOTE] > 🤖 **Agent assistance: gpt-6.1-sol via Codex**

title: feat(accounts): show reset credits for paused accounts
head: 9a9232cff0daeac504fc1e41d3a416569c11a254
body:
## Summary

Allow operators to inspect a paused account's reset-credit count without resuming request routing. The selected-account read uses the existing credential refresh and account-bound proxy path; cached counts remain visible, while polling and both manual/automatic redemption remain blocked.

## Type of change

- [x] `feat:` — new user-facing capability

Linked issue: None. This is a focused operator-requested visibility improvement, not a claim to resolve a broader issue.

## OpenSpec

- [x] Includes a verified, archived OpenSpec change and synchronized main specs.

Change directory: `openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-25-allow-paused-account-reset-credit-visibility/`

Upstream request/response formats and OAuth exchange behavior are unchanged; this changes local dashboard read eligibility only.

## Changes

- Allow the selected paused account's count GET, preserving identity checks, token refresh/401 retry, proxy-route resolution and error envelopes.
- Preserve paused cached count/expiry in account summaries and the cached-detail GET. Weekly reset timestamps similarly remain last-observed data; cached credit badges are not a freshness guarantee.
- Keep request routing, background credit polling, and manual/automatic redemption disabled for paused accounts. Preserve existing deactivated/reauth policies.
- Add API/UI regression coverage and document the observation policy.

## Simplicity

- [x] Works with zero configuration; no new required setup.
- New settings / tiers / migrations: none.
- [x] No README, environment-variable or navigation budget changes.
- [x] Feature documentation lives in `docs/usage-reporting.md` and links to the owning OpenSpec capability.

## Test plan

On upstream main `09a140fa9` plus this change:

```text
make lint                                      passed
make typecheck                                 passed
pytest accounts/reset-credit API+mapper+scheduler suites  123 passed
pytest auth_manager/auth_guardian -k paused       2 passed
vitest account-detail/account-actions/use-accounts       24 passed
git diff --check                               passed
```

The change and reset-credit main spec passed strict OpenSpec validation. Full `openspec validate --specs --strict` reports **49 passed / 17 failed**; these are pre-existing failures (the original base comparison had the identical error map). No new validation errors were introduced. This PR remains draft pending CI/review and resolution or maintainer disposition of that repository-wide gate.

Independent local review found no material issues. Tests cover paused-state preservation, refreshed-token retry, upstream/auth/route failures, cached visibility, and both consume endpoints rejecting paused accounts. The route-failure test stubs the unchanged resolver's fail-closed result. Full local CI/PostgreSQL/Helm suites were not run.

## Screenshots / output

Synthetic before/after API response fixtures rendered in the existing dashboard; no production account or credit consumption. Playwright verified both reset actions remain disabled. These are focused account-view captures, not a complete application smoke test.

| Before: paused read unavailable | After: two credits visible, account still paused |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codemoo/codex-lb/9a9232cff0daeac504fc1e41d3a416569c11a254/docs/screenshots/paused-reset-credits/before.png) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codemoo/codex-lb/9a9232cff0daeac504fc1e41d3a416569c11a254/docs/screenshots/paused-reset-credits/after.png) |

## Checklist

- [x] Conventional Commits title.
- [x] Tests cover the changed product path.
- [x] Relevant local make targets and focused tests ran.
- [ ] Full OpenSpec validation passes — existing 17 failures documented above.
- [x] Simplicity rules P1–P6 reviewed.
- [x] CHANGELOG unchanged; no version bump.

No production deployment or restart is included.

title: fix(warmup): restore reset usage threshold
head: cc5e2478d6c9515d93de6d19209191def5a759b6
body:
## Summary

Restore the dashboard's `Reset-confirmed warm-up / Min usage %` setting as an active, inclusive pre-reset usage gate, defaulting to `0%` so every confirmed reset is eligible.

The setting previously stayed visible but no longer affected reset-confirmed candidate selection. This change makes it meaningful again: `0%` qualifies every confirmed reset, while a positive value requires the prior usage sample to meet that floor.

## Type of change

- [x] `fix:` — bug fix (restores the existing dashboard contract)
- [ ] `feat:` — new user-facing feature or capability
- [ ] `refactor:` — internal refactor
- [ ] `docs:` — documentation only
- [ ] `chore:` / `ci:` / `build:` — tooling, CI, packaging
- [ ] `test:` — test-only change
- [ ] **Breaking change**

Related context: #1504, #1700, and #1825.

## OpenSpec

- [x] This PR includes / updates an OpenSpec change
- [ ] Not applicable — bug fix fully covered by an existing spec
- [ ] This PR touches a codex-faithful path

Change directories: `openspec/changes/restore-limit-warmup-threshold/` and its prerequisite `openspec/changes/stage-limit-warmup-zero-compat/`.

## Changes

- Pass the configured threshold into ordinary reset-confirmed candidate construction and apply it inclusively: a sample qualifies when `before.used_percent >= threshold`.
- Default the setting to `0.0` in the repository defaults, the ORM active column, the backend Pydantic bounds (`ge=0.0`), the frontend Zod bounds (`nonnegative()`), the mocked fixture factory, and the dashboard numeric control (`min=0`). Empty input is still rejected.
- Gate the paid-to-Free monthly transition with the same threshold. With `0%` a missing pre-refresh sample stays eligible; with a positive threshold the fallback fails closed until a prior monthly sample exists and meets the floor.
- Restore the reset-threshold contract in two staged Alembic revisions that chain linearly onto the current `main` head:
  - `20260909_130000_stage_limit_warmup_zero_compat` adds the nullable, unbackfilled `limit_warmup_reset_threshold_percent` column and backfills nothing.
  - `20260906_000000_restore_limit_warmup_threshold_default` initializes every existing row to the requested `0.0` default and makes the active column non-null with a `0.0` server default.
- Map the public Python/API setting to the new active column and keep the legacy `limit_warmup_exhausted_threshold_percent` column mapped internally only to prevent schema drift. Its values and its `99.0` server default are never rewritten.
- Downgrade the activation revision back to the compatibility shape (nullable, no server default, stored value preserved) and let the staged revision drop its own column.
- Preserve reset confirmation, post-reset availability, opt-in, active-account, model, cooldown, sender-preflight, recovery-ordering, and durable deduplication gates.
- Cover the behavior with backend, migration, and frontend regression tests.

## Behavior examples

| Configured threshold | Previous usage | Confirmed reset | Result |
| ---: | ---: | :---: | :--- |
| `0%` | `15%` | yes | Warm-up eligible |
| `50%` | `15%` | yes | Skipped |
| `50%` | `50%` | yes | Warm-up eligible (inclusive boundary) |
| `99%` | `98%` | yes | Skipped |
| `100%` | `100%` | yes | Warm-up eligible |

The threshold does not bypass reset confirmation. A newer usage row must still prove a real reset and satisfy the existing availability and safety gates.

## Migration behavior

`upgrade head` walks the compatibility revision first and the activation revision second, so the two-author chain stays a single head:

- The staged revision only adds the nullable column. It neither backfills nor activates anything, and its downgrade drops only that column.
- The activation revision depends on the staged revision, initializes existing rows to `0.0`, and makes the active column non-null with a `0.0` server default.
- The legacy exhausted-threshold column keeps its stored values and its `99.0` server default throughout. No trigger, dual write, or sentinel is introduced.
- The activation downgrade restores the compatibility shape (nullable, no default) and preserves the stored value; the staged downgrade then removes the column.

The two revisions were re-pointed onto the current `main` head when `main` advanced, so the merged graph has exactly one head and no fork.

No new endpoint, environment variable, dependency, or worker is added by this PR.

## Test plan

```text
uv run pytest -q tests/integration/test_migration_merge_overflow_transport.py tests/unit/test_limit_warmup.py tests/integration/test_settings_api.py tests/unit/test_db_migrate.py
# 248 passed

uv run pytest -q tests/integration/test_migrations.py
# 57 passed, 9 skipped

uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_check_migration_topology.py tests/unit/test_migration_identifier_literals.py
# 37 passed

make migration-check
# current_revision=20260906_000000_restore_limit_warmup_threshold_default
# migration_policy=ok
# schema_drift=none

make architecture-check
# proxy architecture, cancellation safety, timing seams, settings tiers and migration topology checks passed

uv run python scripts/check_migration_topology.py --base-ref upstream/main
# revisions: 262; head: 20260906_000000_restore_limit_warmup_threshold_default
# migration topology checks passed

npx --yes @fission-ai/openspec@1.11.0 validate --specs
# 65 passed, 0 failed

npx --yes @fission-ai/openspec@1.11.0 validate --strict restore-limit-warmup-threshold
npx --yes @fission-ai/openspec@1.11.0 validate --strict stage-limit-warmup-zero-compat
# both changes valid

uv run ruff format --check <changed python files>   # already formatted
uv run ruff check <changed python files>            # all checks passed
python -m compileall <changed python files>         # ok
git diff --check                                    # clean

cd frontend && bun run test src/features/settings/schemas.test.ts src/features/settings/components/routing-settings.test.tsx
# 2 files passed, 79 tests passed
```

Migration regression coverage proves the staged column is nullable, unbackfilled and reversible; that the activation initializes existing rows to `0.0` and lands non-null with a `0.0` default without mutating the legacy column; that legacy-only writes are not synchronized; and that downgrade restores the compatibility shape while preserving the stored active value. The merge-graph test keeps upstream's `check_schema_drift` assertions and additionally pins the `0.0` warm-up default across every settings row.

Warm-up coverage includes below-threshold, inclusive-boundary, zero-threshold, paid-to-Free, and wrong-window prior-history cases. Frontend coverage includes empty-input rejection and explicit-zero acceptance.

## Checklist

- [x] Title is in Conventional Commits format.
- [x] Added OpenSpec proposal, context, design, requirements, and task checklist.
- [x] Restored the threshold's behavior without removing the operator control.
- [x] Kept `0%` as the default all-resets behavior.
- [x] Made upgrade and downgrade data-safe, with the legacy column untouched.
- [x] Re-pointed both revisions onto the current `main` head so the graph keeps a single head.
- [x] Added backend, frontend, migration, graph, and paid-to-Free regression coverage.
- [x] Ran the relevant test, lint, migration, topology and OpenSpec gates.
- [x] No production deploy or runtime configuration change was performed.
- [x] CHANGELOG was not edited by hand.

title: feat(accounts): redeem all eligible reset credits in one action
body:
## Problem / motivation

Operators with many pooled accounts currently redeem banked reset credits one account at a time from the Accounts page, or opt in to automatic redemption shortly before expiry (#1357 / #1358). There is no way to redeem every currently eligible credit in one action. Requested by a user via email (2026-09-17).

## Proposed change

Add a "Redeem all eligible reset credits" action to the Accounts surface that:

- redeems each account's own credits only (no cross-account pooling; see the decision on #2289),
- reuses the existing per-account redeem helper, durable ledger and per-account serialization,
- shows a confirmation listing the accounts and credit counts that will be consumed, and reports per-account success/failure,
- stays default-off in behaviour (it is an explicit operator click, never automatic).

## Out of scope

- Pooling credits across accounts (declined in #2289).
- Changing the auto-redeem scheduler semantics.
